findings.claim: Crude oil and U.S. natural gas have exhibited meaningful linkage, but its strength is time-varying and weakened materially after structural changes including shale-era developments.
findings.expected_direction: positive oil-to-gas linkage is regime-dependent, not a fixed coefficient

findings.claim: The European energy crisis had only a marginal effect on U.S. natural-gas market dynamics in a structural VAR analysis, so Henry Hub should not be assumed to mechanically inherit European gas shocks.
findings.expected_direction: cross-basin transmission is conditional and may be economically small

findings.claim: Evidence from integrated European gas markets shows contemporaneous spillovers dominate lagged spillovers and pipeline congestion weakens connectedness, supporting explicit separation of contemporaneous from forecastable cross-market information.
findings.expected_direction: congestion -> lower connectedness; contemporaneous transmission > lagged transmission

sources.scope: contextual European evidence, not direct Henry Hub proof
